title: Pre-Analysis — Starter Duct Clamping Standard Against the Elevation Start Complaints
abstract: Closed work order asking whether the duct clamping standard already covers the hung starts reported at high elevation, and delegating the answer to a new candidate when it did not.

sections.objective: Establish whether the two-piece clamp and position switch standard, released in 2020 for duct joint fretting, already covers the hung starts that four aircraft are reporting at high field elevation, or whether a further change is needed. The operator had asked why an aircraft that carries the standard still hangs its starts.
sections.findings_summary: The standard does not cover it and was never meant to. It recovers mass flow lost to joint fretting, which is a sea-level warm-day problem, and the elevation cases are a different margin entirely: the supply is already marginal before any loss and the recovered four per cent is not the difference. The evidence for this is in the trouble shooting procedure, which separates the two conditions clearly and which nobody had consulted before raising the question. Two further items came out of the search. The position switch introduced by the standard gives a valve-open discrete but nothing records it, so an engineer reconstructing a hung start still depends on the crew's memory, and that gap is exactly what the operator is complaining about. The crew procedure entry already tells crews to prefer a cross-bleed start at elevation, which is the correct mitigation and which the operator was not applying.
sections.next_steps: Delegate the elevation case to a new candidate rather than amending this standard. Point the operator at the cross-bleed start guidance in the crew procedure as an immediate mitigation. Record the missing recorded parameter as the strongest single requirement for whatever comes next.

similarity_seeds: start hangs below light-up speed at high field elevation
duct joint fretting and mass flow loss

tasks.title: Separate the elevation cases from the fretting cases in the fleet data
Establish what the position switch actually records
Check the crew guidance already published

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity between the operator complaint and the fault description; the procedure and the modification share the clamp part numbers but the discriminating content is entirely textual.

expected_findings.rationale: The trouble shooting procedure already separates the elevation condition from the fretting condition and states that replacing the starter is the common wrong answer. That analysis predates the operator question and answers most of it.
expected_findings.resolution: Quote the procedure to the operator and use it as the baseline for the new candidate.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by similarity alone. The crew entry and the modification share no identifier and are written in entirely different registers.

expected_findings.rationale: The crew procedure already recommends a cross-bleed start at elevation in preference to a second auxiliary power unit start. The operator was not applying it, which is a training question rather than a design one.
expected_findings.resolution: No change to the entry. Raise the guidance with the operator's flight operations department.

evidence.similarity_note: Reached from the modification to its retrofit bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin will need a pre-modification condition against whatever candidate addresses the elevation case, because the two changes touch the same clamps and the same nozzle face.
expected_findings.resolution: Record as a constraint on the new candidate rather than acting now.

type_data.conclusion: Closed and delegated. A new candidate is required; this standard is not the vehicle.
